# Accepted projected whole-digest wrapper

The official positive proof and independent artifact review accepted the complete Result of ObjHashBytes on the original projected 96-byte range, returning the original manifest digest record. Genuine Direct09 source, production Result branches, append/projection conversion and empty observed axioms were checked in the new official closure.

Both phases supplied 18 inputs, including 14 source modules; source checks admitted 11 modules. The positive verified those modules in 113,189 ms aggregate. The artifact contains 115 files, 55 outputs and 11 oleans, with 744 empty-axiom declarations, 34 successful processes and 11 kernel replays. All operational guards passed.

The mandatory false consumer changed only the expected first digest byte from 201 to 202. It was rejected with LLV7002 after 115,437 ms aggregate, without an artifact. The separate correct positive establishes the required wrapper conversion. These durations are aggregate verification times, not isolated theorem timings or speedup evidence.

See the exact [positive review](evidence/positive/positive-native-review.json), [negative review](evidence/negative-native-review.json) and results.json for acceptance custody. The independent census is retained losslessly as inert JSON in independent-artifact-census.json.gz, with compressed and decoded hashes. The earlier author census remains unchanged; file serialization hashes and array digests are distinct identities. Full binary artifacts remain local.

The negative resource observation was post-run, not an active measurement or peak. The corrected parent preflight schema error occurred before launch and was not a native result. Frozen preparation NOT_RUN and raw-custody pending labels retain their historical meaning; current outcomes are here and in results.json.

Acceptance is limited to the actual projected hash wrapper. The failed whole-read continuation remains unaccepted. Complete ObjWholeRead, original ordinal26/Read33, ten drafts, canonical Hash and full PrismPM/Pages integration remain open. No cache, efficiency or full component acceptance is claimed.
